question: The units digit of \(3^{1001}7^{1002}13^{1003}\) is
solution:
Only the units digits of factors affect the units digit of their product: every other contribution is a multiple of \(10\). Consequently, powers of \(13\) have the same units digits as the corresponding powers of \(3\).

The first four powers of \(3\) have units digits \(3,9,7,1\), and the first four powers of \(7\) have units digits \(7,9,3,1\). Since each fourth power ends in \(1\), each additional block of four factors starts the same pattern again.

The exponents \(1001,1002,1003\) leave remainders \(1,2,3\), respectively, when divided by \(4\). Thus \(3^{1001}\), \(7^{1002}\), and \(13^{1003}\) have units digits \(3,9,7\). Finally,
\[
3\cdot9\cdot7=189,
\]
so the required units digit is \(9\), choice E.
